name: Souletin Basque
world_status: statement found in a copy we already had

new_statements.quote: Zuberoan is the only eastern dialect with contrastive accent. The general accentual rule of Zuberoan is penultimate accent, as seen in table 40. [...] However, there is also a marked oxytonic pattern. In some cases, oxytonic accent is clearly the result of a historical contraction. For instance, the absolutive singular form of stems ending in -a, where a historical sequence /a+a/ has been reduced, shows final accent, table 41 (a). Final accent is also found in plural forms of all words, except in the absolutive. [...] There is also a group of monomorphemic words which exceptionally present final instead of penultimate stress (e.g. arrés 'sheep', animál 'huge').
new_statements.citation: Hualde, José Ignacio. 2003. 'Accentuation' (section 2.2; 2.2.4 'Zuberoan'), in José Ignacio Hualde & Jon Ortiz de Urbina (eds.), A Grammar of Basque (Mouton Grammar Library 26), 65-72. Berlin/New York: Mouton de Gruyter.
new_statements.locator: pp. 71-72, sec. 2.2.4 'Zuberoan', with Tables 40-41 (archive.org scan pp. 102-103)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Ran the target print (soul1243 = Glottolog Bookkeeping entry for retired ISO bsz; 0 descriptive refs; we have no copy because the deciding file sits under the the weight-sensitive languages basq1250 cache rather than our files). Opened the named file via its derived extracted text of pp. 102-103) and the rendered page scan and printed pp. 71-72). The quoted passage is on the page word for word: p. 71 bottom '2.2.4. Zuberoan / Zuberoan is the only eastern dialect with contrastive accent. The general accentual rule of Zuberoan is penultimate accent, as seen in table 40.'; p. 72 Table 40 (gízun, gizúna, gizúnak; bezála, bezaláko, bezalakóxe), then 'However, there is also a marked oxytonic patt…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Default word accent on the penultimate syllable of the (inflected) word (gízun, gizúna, gizúnak; bezála, bezaláko, bezalakóxe), i.e. a syllabic trochee at the right edge, weight-insensitive; accent is contrastive because a marked class has final accent: absolutive singular of -a stems (alhabá < *alhaba-a vs uninflected alhába), all non-absolutive plural forms (gizunék, gizunér), words with certain monosyllabic derivational suffixes (aitañí), and a lexical set of monomorphemic oxytones (arrés, animál). Older and Basque-language descriptions agree: Gèze 1873 p. 3 'La syllabe longue est ordinairement la pénultième'; Michelena FHV 20.11 'El tema nominal nudo es por regla general paroxítono'; Hualde 1997 p. 75 'Zubereraz, azentua normalean azkenaurreko silaban ezartzen da'.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described by Hualde 2003/1997 for Zuberoan; Michelena (FHV 20.10, quoting Larrasquet) reports that many words in NE Souletin (Barcus, Esquiule) carry one or two secondary accents of intensity only, without giving their position, and explicitly sets them aside ('No mencionaremos aquí los acentos secundarios').
new_statements.exceptions: Final (oxytonic) accent: (a) ABS SG of -a stems via /a+a/ contraction (alhabá, neská); (b) all plural forms except the absolutive (plural -e-: gizunék, gizunér; Hualde 1997/E&E 2023 add penult gizunéna and antepenult gizonéntako with longer plural suffixes, i.e. -e- attracts stress); (c) certain monosyllabic derivational suffixes (aitañí; -ñí, -xkót, -tiár, -kór, -ús per E&E 2023) and compounds with monosyllabic second member (ollár, gibelmín); (d) lexical monomorphemic oxytones, mostly loans (arrés, animál, buhamí); Hualde 1997 also: words ending in a glide or a nasalized vowel are oxytone (erhói, ardṹ), and some suffixes may stay outside the accent unit yielding proparoxytones.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level contrastive accent; the accentual domain is the inflected word including the article/case suffixes in Zuberoan (vs. the stem in Roncalese, per Hualde 1997 and Egurtzegi & Elordieta 2023); Hualde 1997 4.3.6 notes optionality in non-absolutive singular forms (keep the absolutive's accent gizúnai or re-penultimize gizunái); compounds: each member its own unit, main accent on the second. Gaminde 1995 alternatively analyses a lexeme-final word accent plus a phrase-level penult rule, with village-by-village variation.
new_statements.identity_note: soul1243 'Souletin Basque' is a Glottolog Bookkeeping languoid (retired ISO 639-3 bsz, change request 2006-118, merged into eus 2007-08-10). The lect described by every source here (Zuberoan / zuberera / souletin) is the live Glottolog dialect basq1250 'Souletin' under Basque basq1248, which is ALREADY a catalog unit coded from the same Hualde 2003 sec. 2.2.4 (verified against the source; was ruled duplicate entry of basq1250). by our rule that each source is filed under the language's current Glottolog code (a retired code does not make a separate language) this key should not enter as a second entity; hence not proposed for the catalog despite a first-hand held quote. Sub-dialect notes: Larrasquet/Michelena describe north-eastern (Basse-Soule: Barcus, Esquiule) Souletin; Lafon notes Haute-Soule (Larrau) differences; Gaminde 1995 covers nine villages (Altzai, Altzürükü, Barkoxe, Eskiula, Larrañe, Ligi, Mithikile, Muskildi, Santa Grazi).

sources.citation: Egurtzegi, Ander & Gorka Elordieta. 2023. A history of the Basque prosodic systems. Diachronica 40(1): 30-72. (HAL open postprint)
sources.note: sec. 3.4 'Eastern' p. 54: 'In this system, unmarked stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the base, which is the stem in Roncalese and the word in Zuberoan (e.g., gízun, gizún-a, néska, alhába)'; marked final stress from old vowel clusters (alhabá, neská), monosyllabic suffixes and monosyllabic second compound members; syllabic trochee at right edge of the word; plural -e- attracts stress (gizun-ék, gizun-éna, gizon-éntako).

sources.citation: Hualde, José Ignacio. 2003. 'Accentuation' (sec. 2.2; 2.2.4 'Zuberoan'), in J. I. Hualde & J. Ortiz de Urbina (eds.), A Grammar of Basque (Mouton Grammar Library 26), pp. 65-72. Berlin/New York: Mouton de Gruyter.
sources.note: pp. 71-72: Zuberoan is the only eastern dialect with contrastive accent; general rule = penultimate accent (gízun, gizúna, gizúnak; bezála, bezaláko, bezalakóxe); marked final accent from historical contraction (ABS SG of -a stems alhabá vs uninfl. alhába; all non-absolutive plurals gizunék, gizunér), with certain monosyllabic derivational suffixes (aitañí), and in a group of monomorphemic lexical exceptions (arrés, animál).

sources.citation: Hualde, José Ignacio. 1997. Euskararen azentuerak (ASJU-ren Gehigarriak 42). Bilbo/Donostia: UPV/EHU & Gipuzkoako Foru Aldundia. doi:10.1387/asju.8621 (open).
sources.note: sec. 4.3.1 p. 75: 'Zubereraz, azentua normalean azkenaurreko silaban ezartzen da' (in Zuberoan the accent is normally placed on the penultimate syllable), based on Larrasquet's (1939) dictionary; trochaic foot at right edge; lexical oxytones (arrés, animál..); 4.3.6 summary pp. 84-85: monomorphemic words penult, final if word ends in glide, nasal vowel or is lexically marked; ABS SG penult except -a stems (neská); plural -e- forms final (gizunék); some suffixes extrametrical giving proparoxytones (gizunentako); compounds: each member an accent unit, main accent on second.

sources.citation: Gaminde, Iñaki. 1995. Zubereraren azentuaz. Uztaro 13: 107-128. (open, UEU)
sources.note: Fieldwork in nine Zuberoan villages (1994) with acoustic F0/duration/intensity measures; quotes Michelena (accent regulated from the last syllable, oxytony exceptional, older uniform penult); proposes word accent on the lexeme's last syllable plus a phrase-level rule placing main accent on the penult after affixation (pp. 115-116), noting inter-village differences in declension accent.

sources.citation: Michelena, Luis. 1961 [2nd ed. 1977; repr. 1990]. Fonética histórica vasca (Anejos de ASJU 4; Obras completas de Luis Michelena I). Donostia/San Sebastián: Gipuzkoako Foru Aldundia. doi:10.1387/asju.8531 (open).
sources.note: cap. 20 sec. 20.10-20.11 pp. 392-393: summarizes Larrasquet (NE Souletin accent musical+intensity, fixed per word); 'En cuanto a su posición, en un texto continuo predominan las palabras paroxítonas.. El tema nominal nudo es por regla general paroxítono. Los oxítonos se pueden clasificar en tres grupos' (loans, compounds with monosyllabic last member / accented suffixes, contractions); suffixation moves accent rightward (gízun, gizúna); accent position has morphological value (alhába vs alhabá, gizúnek vs gizunék); 'La oxitonía presupone siempre contracción'.

sources.citation: Gèze, Louis. 1873. Éléments de grammaire basque, dialecte souletin, suivis d'un vocabulaire basque-français & français-basque. Bayonne: Imprimerie Veuve Lamaignère.
sources.note: p. 3 'Accent': 'Dans tout mot de plusieurs syllabes, il en est une sur laquelle la voix doit appuyer plus que sur les autres.. La syllabe longue est ordinairement la pénultième, mais il y a de nombreuses exceptions qu'en l'absence de traité spécial l'usage seul peut apprendre.' Also p. 20 (indefinite vs definite sg of -a stems distinguished by displacement of the tonic accent) and p. 58 (zihâurec accent on 2nd syllable vs plural zihauréc accent on last).
